subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Conduction, Convection, and Radiation.

hook.text: Heat reaches coffee beans through three methods: conduction, convection, and radiation. Each affects flavor differently.

buildup.text: Conduction is direct contact—beans touching the hot drum. Convection is hot air flowing through. Radiation is infrared energy.

discovery.text: Most drum roasters use 60–70% convection and 30–40% conduction. Pure convection creates cleaner, brighter cups.

twist.text: Too much conduction scorches the exterior before the interior develops. The bean looks roasted but tastes raw inside.

climax.text: Balancing all three heat types is the roaster's fundamental skill. It determines evenness, development, and final character.

punchline.text: Three kinds of heat, one perfect balance. Roasting is thermal engineering.

quiz.question: What happens if there is too much conduction during roasting?
options: The exterior scorches before the interior develops properly

details.summary: Coffee roasting uses three heat transfer methods: conduction from the hot drum surface, convection from moving hot air, and radiation from the heated walls. The ratio of these three determines how quickly and evenly the beans roast.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding heat transfer modes helps roasters diagnose problems and replicate profiles across different machines. It is the physics behind every roast decision.
takeaways: Conduction transfers heat where beans touch the hot drum surface
Convection uses moving air to heat beans uniformly
Radiation emits infrared energy from the drum walls to the beans

faq.question: Which heat transfer method has the most impact on flavor?
faq.answer: Conduction has the strongest immediate impact because it creates intense surface heat on contact, which can scorch beans if not managed. Convection is preferred for even development and cleaner cup profiles.

faq.question: Does the drum material affect heat transfer in coffee roasting?
faq.answer: Yes. Cast iron drums retain and radiate more heat, while stainless steel conducts heat faster and responds more quickly to gas adjustments. Each material requires different profiling approaches.
